readme:
# iCIMS Jobs Scraper: Career Sites

Get the open jobs of companies that hire through [iCIMS](https://www.icims.com). Paste a career site URL such as `https://careers.axa.com` and receive title, company, location, apply URL and, when the site provides them, department, employment type, description and posting date as clean dataset rows.

## What you can do with it

- Pull the open roles of a list of target companies for lead generation or recruiting research.
- Track hiring over time: run it on a schedule with `postedWithinDays` and `sortBy: newest` to see only new postings.
- Feed a job board or alert system with the openings of the companies you follow.
- Filter by keyword in the title, by location or by country.

## What you get

One dataset row per job. Duplicates are removed before anything is charged, so the number of rows is the number of results you pay for.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | Job id, unique across career sites |
| `ats_job_id` | The id the career site itself uses for the posting |
| `title` | Job title |
| `company` | Employer name as the posting states it (for example `Costco Wholesale Corporation`) |
| `company_legacy` | Original company name as the site wrote it, only when the company name was normalised (for example a trailing number removed) |
| `hiring_organization` | The legal entity the posting names, when the career site reports one |
| `ats_platform` | `icims_jibe` (Jibe career site) or `icims` (iCIMS portal) |
| `location`, `city`, `country` | Location text as posted, the city and the two-letter country code |
| `additional_locations` | The other places of a posting that lists several, when the site provides them |
| `department` | Department or category, when the site provides it |
| `employment_type` | Full-time, part-time, contract and so on, when the site provides it |
| `remote` | `true` when the location says remote |
| `description` | The posting text as the site provides it (HTML or plain text, depending on the career site). Empty when `includeDescription` is off or the posting has none |
| `apply_url`, `job_url` | Link to the application page and to the posting |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | Posting date and last update, when the site provides them |
| `language` | Language of the posting, when the site provides it |
| `scraped_at` | Time of the run |

Salary fields (`salary_text`, `salary_min`, `salary_max`, `salary_currency`, `salary_period`, `salary_source`) are filled only when the posting states a salary range. They are never estimated.

## Input

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `companies` | iCIMS career site URLs (`https://careers.axa.com`; the home page, a list page or a posting link all work). Strings, `{"url": "..."}` objects, a single string, or several separated by commas or new lines. Empty = one public sample career site; a run with no input returns up to 10 sample jobs. |
| `ats` | `auto` (default) recognises iCIMS portal URLs and checks any other URL for a Jibe career site. Set `icims_jibe` to read a URL as a Jibe career site on the company's own domain. |
| `keywords` | Keep only jobs whose title matches at least one keyword. They filter the jobs of the sites you list; they do not search other companies. |
| `location` | Keep only jobs in this city, region or country (`Geneva`, `Switzerland`, `CH`). |
| `countries` | ISO-2 codes such as `["CH", "DE"]`: keep only jobs located in these countries (jobs whose country cannot be determined are left out). |
| `includeRemoteWithoutRegion` | Only with a country filter: also keep remote jobs that state no country or region (they may not be open to applicants in that country). Default `false`. |
| `postedWithinDays` | Drop jobs older than this many days. Jobs without a posting date are kept. |
| `sortBy` | `newest` (default) or `relevance` (the site's own order). |
| `maxJobsPerCompany` | Cap per career site, counted after the filters. `0` = all. Default 50. |
| `maxResults` | Cap for the whole run. The run stops cleanly when it is reached. `0` = no limit. Default 100 (10 when `companies` is empty and you pass no `maxResults`). |
| `includeDescription` | Include the description text. Default `true`. |

Large career sites hold thousands of jobs (Costco lists about 20,000). The default of 50 jobs per career site keeps a run small and cheap; raise `maxJobsPerCompany` and `maxResults` only when you want more.

### Example: one career site

```json
{
  "companies": ["https://careers.axa.com"],
  "maxResults": 20
}
```

### Example: several career sites with filters

```json
{
  "companies": [
    "https://careers.costco.com",
    "https://jobs.booking.com"
  ],
  "keywords": ["engineer", "data"],
  "postedWithinDays": 30,
  "sortBy": "newest",
  "maxJobsPerCompany": 25
}
```

Only iCIMS career sites are read. A URL of any other job system (Greenhouse, Workday, SmartRecruiters and so on) is skipped with a log line that names the actor to use, and is never charged.

### Supported URL formats

- Jibe career site: the home page, a list page or a posting link of the company's own career domain, for example `https://careers.costco.com` or `https://jobs.booking.com/booking/jobs`. A link to one posting is reduced to its career site; the whole site is read.
- iCIMS portal: `https://careers-company.icims.com/jobs/search`. Some iCIMS portals put their job search behind a human-verification check. For those the run status says so and suggests the company's own career site URL, and nothing is pushed or charged. Jibe career sites are the reliable case.
- A bare company name is not enough, because the career site address is needed.

## Output

```json
{
  "id": "icims_jibe-a1b2c3d4-67964",
  "ats_job_id": "67964",
  "title": "Pharmacy Manager",
  "company": "Costco Wholesale Corporation",
  "hiring_organization": "Costco Wholesale Corporation",
  "ats_platform": "icims_jibe",
  "location": "ALBUQUERQUE, New Mexico, United States",
  "city": "Albuquerque",
  "country": "US",
  "department": "Warehouses and Business Associates",
  "employment_type": null,
  "remote": false,
  "apply_url": "https://pharmacycareers-costco.icims.com/jobs/67964/login",
  "job_url": "https://careers.costco.com/jobs/67964?lang=en-us",
  "language": "en",
  "created_at": "2026-10-21T19:38:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-22T07:40:59Z",
  "scraped_at": "2026-10-27T09:00:00Z"
}
```

The row above is illustrative and comes from a different career site than the sample one an empty input reads (the description field is left out for brevity); values depend on the career site. Fields a career site does not provide stay empty. `created_at` is the posting date the career site reports.

## Pricing

Pay per result, two events:

- `apify-actor-start`: $0.001 once per run.
- `job-result`: $0.001 per job in the dataset ($1.00 per 1,000 jobs).

The start fee is charged on top of the job results. Filtered-out and duplicate jobs are never charged, and a site that is not found costs nothing. Set a maximum total charge on the run to stop at a budget; the run ends cleanly when it is reached. The pricing box on the actor page always shows the current rates.

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Example prompts once connected:**

> "Use `icims-jobs-scraper` for https://careers.axa.com and list the open roles with title, location and apply URL."

> "Use `icims-jobs-scraper` for https://jobs.booking.com and return the roles posted in the last 30 days."

Configure the MCP server with the iCIMS Jobs Scraper preconfigured at `mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/icims-jobs-scraper`:

```json
{
    "mcpServers": {
        "apify": {
            "command": "npx",
            "args": [
                "mcp-remote",
                "https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=santamaria-automations/icims-jobs-scraper",
                "--header",
                "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_TOKEN>"
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

See the auto-generated API tab on the actor page for language-specific examples (cURL, JavaScript, Python, and more).

## FAQ

**How do I find a company's iCIMS career site URL?**
Open the company's careers page. If the jobs are listed on the company's own career domain and the apply button leads to an `icims.com` page, it is an iCIMS career site and the career domain is the URL to use. If a URL is not recognised, set `ats` to `icims_jibe`.

**Can I search by keyword across all iCIMS companies?**
No. Give the URL of each career site. Keywords only filter the titles of the jobs of the sites you list.

**What if a career site is not found?**
The run continues with the other sites. The run status line names the site and the reason, and nothing is charged for it.

**Why is the description empty?**
It is empty when `includeDescription` is off, or when the posting could not be read. The row still has title, location, date and the apply URL, and is charged the same.

**How do I get only new jobs?**
Run it on a schedule with `postedWithinDays` set to the interval (for example `1` for a daily run) and `sortBy` set to `newest`.

**How do I stop at a budget?**
Set `maxResults` or the maximum total charge of the run. The run stops cleanly when either is reached.

**Why did I get fewer jobs than `maxJobsPerCompany`?**
The caps apply after your filters, and a career site can simply have fewer open jobs. The sites are read in the order you list them, and the run stops once `maxResults` is reached.

## Limits

- Career sites only; no company-name search across iCIMS.
- iCIMS portal URLs (`*.icims.com`) are accepted, but some of those portals put their job search behind a human-verification check and then return nothing. Use the company's own career site URL for those when it has one.
- Salary fields are filled only when the posting states a salary, and only with `includeDescription` on.
